entities.summary:
Antoine-Louis Rouillé, comte de Jouy, was a French statesman and comte of Jouy-en-Josas.

Born into a noble family, Rouillé was educated in law and politics, eventually becoming a prominent figure in the French government.

He played a crucial role in the French Revolution, serving as a member of the Estates-General and later as a delegate to the National Assembly.

Rouillé's influence extended beyond politics, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the works of prominent writers, including Voltaire.

He died on September 20, 1761, leaving behind a legacy as a key figure in French history during the 18th century.

Rouillé's impact on French society can still be seen in the many cultural and political institutions he helped establish, including the National Assembly and the Comte de Jouy-en-Josas estate.

The Comte de Jouy-en-Josas estate, once his family's seat, now serves as a museum and testament to Rouillé's enduring influence on French history.

Antoine-Louis Rouillé, comte de Jouy, was a French statesman and comte of Jouy-en-Josas.

Born on June 7, 1689, in Paris, France, Rouillé rose to prominence in the French government during the early 18th century.

Rouillé's career was marked by his involvement in the French Enlightenment, during which he advocated for constitutional reforms and the establishment of the French Academy of Sciences.

As a key figure in the French Enlightenment, Rouillé's ideas influenced the development of modern French politics and education.

Despite his contributions to French society, Rouillé's legacy is often overshadowed by his contemporaries, such as Voltaire and Rousseau.

Rouillé's life serves as a reminder of the complexities of French history during this period, a time marked by intellectual ferment and political upheaval.

The intersection of science, philosophy, and politics in 18th-century France continues to captivate historians and scholars today.
